panels.body: We have a soft spot for Philly people and passionate creators. With a successful track record and a clear, vibrant vision for their future, REC Philly’s leadership team is focused and driven. Their ability to articulate their mission combined with our ability to supercharge their business with digital strategy and support have made them a perfect Ventures partner.

With its expanded space and evolution of its business, REC Philly required an overhaul of key procedures and technology. By mapping out their customer journey, we defined key criteria for choosing a technology solution that fit their go-to-market needs and is flexible enough to account for the customizations necessary to support their future vision.

While our MVP solution will be a big step forward for REC’s members, we’re hyper-focused on enabling the future of its organization by empowering new features and functionality that make it easier to book time in the space and connect with fellow artists. Our plan is to develop a tight user feedback loop that will account for member insight as each new feature comes online.

sections.heading: Investing in exceptional people, products + experiences

migration.provisionalNote: No canonical Figma frame exists for a venture detail page, so the composition is assembled from existing blocks rather than transcribed — hence no figmaNode. Every line of copy is carried from the WordPress `ventures` post (wpId 5902), whose three ACF text blocks become the three rail panels; their kickers are shouted by the old template's `type-kicker` class and are normalized to sentence case here. The band heading ("A Philly venture partner") and the closing CTA are the only unsourced words on the page — WordPress gives the panels no heading and the page no CTA. The copy is also stale in one place a reviewer has to settle: it describes the MVP as still ahead ("our MVP solution will be a big step forward"), and the /ventures page says the REC work has since become Scarlet AI. Cleared by a commissioned frame and an owner confirming where the engagement actually stands. Nothing links here yet, on either site: the WordPress /ventures page names the venture but points at a perspective or a case study instead, so this URL has always been reachable only from search.
